name: purebasic
description: PureBasic language support for Visual Studio Code: code completion, hover, signature help and document outline.

purebasic.completion.keywords.description: Offer language keywords (Procedure, If, ForEach, ...) in completion.

purebasic.completion.builtins.description: Offer built-in library commands (MessageRequester, AddElement, ...) in completion.

purebasic.completion.snippets.description: Insert a call snippet with parameter placeholders for commands that have parameters.

purebasic.completion.minChars.description: How many characters to type before the completion list appears. 0 offers it as soon as you type. A type or member list after '.' or '\' is never held back, and Ctrl+Space follows the same minimum.

purebasic.index.workspace.description: Offer symbols from files joined to this one by IncludeFile/XIncludeFile, directly or through any number of further includes.

purebasic.index.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of workspace files to index, and the cap on one include group.

purebasic.keywords.path.description: Path to a KeywordsData.pbi from the PureBasic IDE source. Set it and any reserved word it has that this extension does not is picked up at startup, so a new PureBasic's keywords do not wait for a new release here. The file does not ship with a PureBasic installation (it belongs to the IDE source); the words are offered in completion straight away, and added to the grammar so they are coloured after a window reload. Leave empty to use only the keywords built in.

purebasic.compiler.path.markdownDescription: The `pbcompiler` to run. Empty uses the one in the PureBasic installation, then `pbcompiler` on the PATH.

purebasic.compiler.debugger.markdownDescription: Compile with the debugger (`-d`). This is what makes `Debug` print and runtime errors report a line; without it they are compiled out.

enumDescriptions: A console application (`-cl`), which keeps its output attached to the terminal.
purebasic.compiler.executableFormat.description: The format Compile writes. The IDE's three choices on macOS: MacOS, Console, Shared .dylib.

purebasic.compiler.subsystem.markdownDescription: Library subsystem to use (`-s`). Empty uses the default one.

purebasic.compiler.outputPath.markdownDescription: Where Compile writes the executable. Empty writes it beside the source, named after it.

purebasic.compiler.commandLine.markdownDescription: Arguments to start the program with. Empty runs it straight from the compiler; set, the program is built first and then started with these.

purebasic.compiler.quiet.markdownDescription: Pass `-q`, so the terminal shows only errors rather than the compiler's progress.

purebasic.format.canonicalCase.description: When formatting, restore the manual's spelling of keywords and library commands (EndProcedure, ReDim, ForEach) and leave your own names as written.

purebasic.trace.server.description: Trace language service activity to the PureBasic output channel (for troubleshooting).

commands.title: PureBasic: Diagnose Completion at the Cursor

commands.//: The same button in green while the debugger is on: a file icon keeps its own colour, which a codicon cannot. Two commands rather than one command in two menu entries, because the icon belongs to the command -- the way the built-in markdown preview does it -- and because two entries for one command id are not reliably shown as two.

scripts.generate: npm run gen-data && npm run gen-grammar
scripts.build: node tools/gen-grammar.mjs && node tools/gen-builtins-ts.mjs && node esbuild.mjs
scripts.check: npm run typecheck && node tools/gen-grammar.mjs --check && node tools/gen-builtins-ts.mjs --check && npm run build
